## What you can do

With the Mothlog MCP (in parentheses, the same action with the API):

- Assign it to yourself when you start on it: `assign_issue` with `{"issue_id": 4, "assignee": "me"}` (`POST /api/0/issues/4/assignee`). Yours, with `list_issues` and `assigned:me`.
- When the fix is done but not deployed yet, mark it resolved in the next release: `set_issue_status` with `{"issue_id": 4, "status": "resolved_next", "comment": "what was fixed and where"}` (`POST /api/0/issues/4/status`). It becomes resolved when a release later than fixture-release-1 is deployed; if it happens again in a later one, it reopens as a regression.
- Mark it resolved now (fix deployed): `set_issue_status` with `{"issue_id": 4, "status": "resolved", "comment": "..."}`.
- Record what you saw or did: `add_comment` with `{"issue_id": 4, "body": "..."}` in Markdown (`POST /api/0/issues/4/comments/`).
- Silence it if there is nothing to fix: `set_issue_status` with `"status": "silenced"` and a `comment` saying why.
- To learn more: `list_events` and `get_event` (other events), `get_issue_tags` (all tags), `get_release` (what a release brought) and `list_comments` (the history).

## What you can do

With the Mothlog MCP (in parentheses, the same action with the API):

- Assign it to yourself when you start on it: `assign_issue` with `{"issue_id": 5, "assignee": "me"}` (`POST /api/0/issues/5/assignee`). Yours, with `list_issues` and `assigned:me`.
- When the fix is done but not deployed yet, mark it resolved in the next release: `set_issue_status` with `{"issue_id": 5, "status": "resolved_next", "comment": "what was fixed and where"}` (`POST /api/0/issues/5/status`). It becomes resolved when a release later than fixture-release-1 is deployed; if it happens again in a later one, it reopens as a regression.
- Mark it resolved now (fix deployed): `set_issue_status` with `{"issue_id": 5, "status": "resolved", "comment": "..."}`.
- Record what you saw or did: `add_comment` with `{"issue_id": 5, "body": "..."}` in Markdown (`POST /api/0/issues/5/comments/`).
- Silence it if there is nothing to fix: `set_issue_status` with `"status": "silenced"` and a `comment` saying why.
- To learn more: `list_events` and `get_event` (other events), `get_issue_tags` (all tags), `get_release` (what a release brought) and `list_comments` (the history).

- Mark it resolved now (fix deployed): `set_issue_status` with `{"issue_id": 7, "status": "resolved", "comment": "..."}`.

- Silence it if there is nothing to fix: `set_issue_status` with `"status": "silenced"` and a `comment` saying why.

## What you can do

With the Mothlog MCP (in parentheses, the same action with the API):

- Assign it to yourself when you start on it: `assign_issue` with `{"issue_id": 8, "assignee": "me"}` (`POST /api/0/issues/8/assignee`). Yours, with `list_issues` and `assigned:me`.
- When the fix is done but not deployed yet, mark it resolved in the next release: `set_issue_status` with `{"issue_id": 8, "status": "resolved_next", "comment": "what was fixed and where"}` (`POST /api/0/issues/8/status`). It becomes resolved when a release later than prueba-upload is deployed; if it happens again in a later one, it reopens as a regression.
- Mark it resolved now (fix deployed): `set_issue_status` with `{"issue_id": 8, "status": "resolved", "comment": "..."}`.
- Record what you saw or did: `add_comment` with `{"issue_id": 8, "body": "..."}` in Markdown (`POST /api/0/issues/8/comments/`).
- Silence it if there is nothing to fix: `set_issue_status` with `"status": "silenced"` and a `comment` saying why.
- To learn more: `list_events` and `get_event` (other events), `get_issue_tags` (all tags), `get_release` (what a release brought) and `list_comments` (the history).
